source_image_dir: Folder of raw training images — each with a matching .txt caption sidecar. The caching step resizes these into post_image_dataset/resized/ and writes the VAE/text/PE caches under post_image_dataset/lora/. This is a preprocess-only knob: training never reads it (it reads the resized + cached outputs). Saved to configs/preprocess.toml; a preset/method file can still override it per-run, and a legacy copy left in base.toml still wins (backward compatible).
drop_lowres_images: When on, source images smaller than the 'Min pixels' threshold below are skipped during preprocessing so they never enter the resize / VAE / text caches — under-sized images add little signal and waste cache space. Turn off to keep every image regardless of size (equivalent to --min_pixels 0). Saved to configs/preprocess.toml.
caption_shuffle_variants: Number of caption variants generated per image during text-encoder caching. v0 is the pristine original caption; v1..v(N-1) are smart-shuffled (the @artist prefix and 'On the …' / 'In the …' section anchors are preserved). The dataloader picks v0 with 20% probability and v1..v(N-1) uniformly otherwise — but only when use_shuffled_caption_variants=true in your method config. Set to 0 to cache a single pristine caption only.
caption_tag_dropout_rate: Per-tag dropout probability applied only to v1..v(N-1) shuffle variants. Tags up to and including the first @artist marker are never dropped — the artist tag is structurally important and the rating/character/series prefix is order-sensitive. Ignored when shuffle variants ≤ 0. Typical: 0.05–0.15. Higher values teach the LoRA to generalize across missing tags but can dilute the signal.
caption_autotag: Run the Anima Tagger over the whole dataset and write '.txt' caption sidecars into the caption master (image_dataset/). This is the batch counterpart to the Dataset tab's per-image autotag button. It runs first in the pipeline — immediately after resize — because every other caption stage (position clauses, order correction, trigger word, text-encoder caching) edits captions this stage may have just created. Tagging reads the resized image, since that is the pixel data training actually sees, but the caption lands next to the original. GPU stage: one tagger pass over the dataset; the checkpoint is downloaded automatically on first use. Caption edits do not invalidate the text-encoder caches, so inside this pipeline the stage always writes and the chained TE step re-encodes afterwards. To review before committing, run `make caption-autotag` in a terminal — that is a dry run by default and leaves post_image_dataset/captions/autotag/report.json with the before/after for every image.
caption_position_clauses: Detect the subjects in a multi-subject image with SAM3, tag each mask-blanked crop with the Anima Tagger, and append positional clauses to the caption in the dataset's hand-written convention: '<flat tags>. On the left, akita neru, yellow eyes. On the right, kasane teto.' The clause binds an attribute to a subject, which the flat tag bag cannot do — the base model already obeys these clauses, so this reinforces an existing conditioning channel rather than teaching a new one. A tag bound to exactly one subject is MOVED out of the flat tag bag into its clause, so each attribute is asserted once, where it belongs — that is what the hand-written captions do (their only tags appearing in both places are character names, which stay in the bag as the cast list). A tag is kept flat when it is shared, when it is a character-invariant attribute the caption gives only one value of (two views of one girl are not two girls), or when the runner-up crop scored too close to call; then it is simply bound and flat at once, never wrongly deleted. `make caption-position ARGS="--flatten --apply"` undoes a run. A clause carries only what tells its subject apart (any tag every crop shares is suppressed), so a '1girl, multiple views' outfit sheet gets maid / bunny / bikini per view instead of the same name and hair four times. Candidates are captions with 'multiple views' or a girls-count > 1; images that already carry clauses, or where detection disagrees with that count, are skipped and logged. This writes the caption next to the RESIZED image (post_image_dataset/) and never the image_dataset/ master — clauses are generated data, so your hand-written captions stay exactly as they are. It runs before caption correction, variants and text-encoder caching, so the correction pass re-buckets the flat bag around the clauses and the new caption is what gets encoded. GPU stage (SAM3 + tagger) — for a review pass before writing anything, run `make caption-position` from a terminal: it is dry-run by default and writes post_image_dataset/captions/position/report.json, plus the exact crops the tagger saw with --crops.
run_sam_mask: Whether 'Run masking' runs SAM3 segmentation at all. Each mask rule below is one SAM3 pass; their masks are unioned into post_image_dataset/masks/. Unchecked, the Run masking button does nothing.
